endorsements.quote: It must handle disclosure of imminent risk with clear protocols for escalation.
Human oversight and shared governance should feed back into model evaluation, audit logs, privacy rules, and updates to safety thresholds.
Escalation pathways should connect risk states to human review, crisis services, emergency protocols, and, when consented and legally permissible, caregiver involvement.

unlisted_practices: Design interactive self-harm AI as a bridge to human care with explicit mechanisms for transition to human support rather than as a standalone alternative.
Disclose to users that the system is an AI, that it does not replace clinical care, and that its understanding of the person's self-harm is partial and provisional.
Constrain interactive mental health AI with a cognitive and safety layer that limits functional inquiry, prohibits method elaboration, and detects imminent risk.
Evaluate conversational AI safety using trajectory-based assessment of whole conversations rather than only endpoint checks of individual responses.

Design guardrails that interrupt validation-seeking patterns, shift from functional exploration to alternative generation, set hard boundaries on method discussion, and encourage human help-seeking at regular intervals.
Prototype and test interactive self-harm AI under controlled, clinically supervised conditions with prospective validation before deployment in self-harm populations.
Prefer active multimodal data collection that flows through the interaction over passive ambient sensing.

Treat emotional signals from multimodal AI as prompts for contextual inquiry rather than stand-alone clinical evidence, and specify how uncertain signals are weighted and overridden by human judgment.
Design self-harm AI systems with regulatory review, clinical governance, and post-deployment monitoring from the outset.
Interactive NSSI systems should directly assess current suicidal intent and acute risk.
Involve caregivers and stakeholders in the design, use, and governance of digital suicide-prevention tools.
Address consent, user control, privacy, and data governance for the narrative data generated by interactive assessment.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual perspective and research agenda outlining a system architecture (combining conversational agent, safety layers, and escalation pathways) for generative AI in self-harm/NSSI rather than an empirical evaluation.
